Definition: from G2556; to injure; figuratively, to exasperate:--make evil affected, entreat evil, harm, hurt, vex.
BiblicalUsage: Kakoo is to injure, to make evil-affected — to turn minds against the good. Pharaoh dealt subtly with Israel and afflicted their fathers; the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and made their minds evil affected against the brethren; and Peter asks, who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word names a real danger: minds can be poisoned against the truth by a word in the ear. The answer is not fear but doing good — no one can truly harm the one who follows what is good.
